checks: Pre-execution commit, frozen registration, started markers, probe and worker receipts are bound by matching hashes.
Synthetic probe reports project venv and current process membership in the named Job; both probe and worker supervisors report successful cleanup and reaped launcher.
Frozen code reads one immutable cache snapshot, checks its registered SHA, loads two registered models and checks their hashes after load and scoring; no holdout or game data is an input.
Worker reports 400 completed CPU forwards on 200 groups, 9694 candidate rows per model and 19388 total; runner progress reports 400 started and completed.
Operation counts total 200; model top-1 and per-operation rates/ranks recomputed from aggregate totals; paired counts 143 both, 31 new-only, 8 old-only and 18 neither are consistent.
limitations: Receipt and frozen-code review only: no independent archive/model byte hash, selected-row reconstruction, score computation, inference, training or game.
One snapshot, model identity and CPU execution are worker-reported/control-flow facts, not independently observed execution.
The new model trained on these groups, old exposure may differ; 166 of 200 teacher operations are WATER and only five FERTILIZE, so no generalization or economic causality follows.
Job memory sampling is not a hard limit, thread settings are requests, and pre/post hashes cannot exclude transient replacement followed by restoration.
No held-out records, GPU, additional training or matches are used on the reviewed code path; absence is based on scope and receipts.
